To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the aurora can be used to monitor the topology of the interconnection between the magnetosheath and the magnetosphere.

(1) the aurora can monitor the topology of magnetosheath/magnetosphere magnetic connections, (2) the cusp is the region where the two types of connections are most likely to coexist, (3) this coexistence is due to the time required for the topology to adjust to a change in the IMF, (4) this time is ~ 3–5 min under the high speed solar wind of 4 January 95, and (5) the motion of the
the magnetosheath cusp aurora and the plasma sheet outer edge are two distinct phenomena that can be observed simultaneously in the aurora.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the topology of the magnetic field lines connecting the magnetosheath with the magnetosphere.
the topology and dynamics of the magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling system.
the topology of the magnetospheric magnetic field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a strong southward rotation (from 5 to - 6 nT) of the interplanetary magnetic field caused an abrupt reorganization of the magnetospheric magnetic field topology and plasma convection.
the auroral observations of the 4 Jan. 1995 event are consistent with the hypothesis that the magnetosphere is reconfiguring from a northward IMF to a southward IMF topology.

the cusp is a dynamic structure, which is not only the source region of magnetosheath ions, but also a region where the magnetic field topology is reconfigured by the interaction of the magnetosheath with the magnetosphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetopause and magnetosphere can be reconfigured within 3–4 minutes, and this can be monitored by the aurora.
the magnetopause and its associated current systems are the key players in controlling the dynamics and topology of the magnetosphere, and in particular the magnetospheric convection and the aurora.
the magnetosphere is an open dynamical system, which responds to the external driving by the solar wind and the internal dynamics of the magnetospheric plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aurora can be a powerful tool to monitor the magnetosheath/magnetosphere topology and its evolution in time.
the aurora is a very powerful tool for monitoring magnetosphere-solar wind coupling.
local auroral observations can be used to monitor the topology of the magnetic field lines connecting the magnetosphere to the solar wind.
